stops.title: City of Delano - Presidents & Mayors
stops.summary: For 150 years, Delano’s story has been shaped not only by the events that changed the community, but by the people who stepped forward to lead it. From the village presidents of its earliest days to the mayors of the modern city, each generation faced its own challenges and made decisions that helped build the Delano we know today. Streets were laid out, wells dug, lights turned on, water and sewer systems built, parks established, and public buildings raised as a small Minnesota village steadily grew into a thriving city. The stories of Delano’s mayors and village presidents offer a glimpse at that journey—and at the local leaders whose service, vision, and everyday decisions helped guide the community through 150 years of change.

stops.title: Delano Community Development Corporation
stops.subtitle: EST. 1967
stops.summary: In 1967, a group of Delano entrepreneurs and business leaders came together with a shared goal: to bring jobs, industry, and new opportunities to their community. They formed the Delano Community Development Corporation (DCDC), combining private investment, local leadership, and innovative development tools to help shape Delano’s future. Their efforts contributed to projects ranging from industrial development and new businesses to housing for the community’s seniors, leaving an impact that continued long after the organization disbanded in 1980. The story of the DCDC is a remarkable example of what can happen when local citizens invest not only in their businesses, but in the future of their hometown.

body.html: In 1967, a group of Delano entrepreneurs and business leaders came together with a shared goal: to bring jobs, industry, and new opportunities to their community. They formed the Delano Community Development Corporation (DCDC), combining private investment, local leadership, and innovative development tools to help shape Delano’s future. Their efforts contributed to projects ranging from industrial development and new businesses to housing for the community’s seniors, leaving an impact that continued long after the organization disbanded in 1980. The story of the DCDC is a remarkable example of what can happen when local citizens invest not only in their businesses, but in the future of their hometown.

The DCDC was a group of entrepreneurs and businessmen who worked to bring jobs to Delano and a better quality of life to Delano.  It was formed in 1967 by Gordy Wetter and Don Gilmer, and organized as a regular business corporation. The leadership team included Virgil Amundsen, Phil Carlberg, Lloyd Griep, Jim Herzog, Jim Iten, Gary Janish, Jean Johnson, Jim Lundsten, Dave Robinson, Mary Robinson, and Lloyd Sell.  100 shares were sold for $100 each.  If you bought a share, you had to either pass it on to your family, or sell it back to the DCDC, which would then sell it.
   The success of the DCDC was made possible with tax increment financing (TIF), a public financing method that is used as a subsidy for redevelopment, infrastructure, and other community-improvement projects. Delano was early to participate in TIF, thus allowing it to avoid the competition from other cities that came later on.  Because the City of Delano was willing to sponsor TIF, the DCDC was able to accomplish many of its goals.
   The Delano Manor was the original reason why DCDC was founded. Currently, in 2021, known as The Estates at Delano, its success served as the basis for other projects.  The creation of the Industrial Park brought several businesses to Delano.  Industrial Louvers came in 1970, with Landscape Structures and Aaron soon after.  The DCDC disbanded and sold out in the late 1980’s/early 1990’s after accomplishing their original mission.

stops.title: Delano - Franklin Township Area Historical Society
stops.subtitle: Est. 1999
stops.summary: Founded in 1999, the Delano Franklin Township Area Historical Society , (DFTAHS) is dedicated to preserving the artifacts, stories, and historical record of Delano and Franklin Township, with a mission to “preserve the past, enrich the present, and secure the future.” After years without a permanent home, the Society established the historic former Delano City Hall as the Delano Franklin Heritage Center and became an active part of community life through Heritage Festivals, workshops, lectures, exhibits, and educational programs. The Heritage Center later became the heart of the Spirit of Community Trail , helping visitors discover the people, businesses, and buildings that shaped Delano. Although water damage during construction forced the museum to close for renovation, the Society continues its work throughout the community, with a grand reopening of the restored Heritage Center targeted for 2027.

The Heritage Center later became the heart of the Spirit of Community Trail, helping visitors discover the people, businesses, and buildings that shaped Delano. Although water damage during construction forced the museum to close for renovation, the Society continues its work throughout the community, with a grand reopening of the restored Heritage Center targeted for 2027.

The Delano Franklin Township Area Historical Society was founded in 1999 with these charter members: Jean Johnson, Frances Johnson, Marla Frach, George Fake, Leona Fake, Kathy Mass, John Steinmetz, Leonard Ludescher, June Sutton, Mildred Shrode, Jim Lundsten, and Lyle Compton.

The purpose of the Historical Society is to acquire artifacts and historical data of the history of Delano and Franklin Township. Its mission is to preserve the past, enrich the present, and secure the future.

The Society did not have a permanent home for many years, meeting in St. Peter’s church basement, and then hoping to secure the Delano Eagle building to house a museum and an art gallery. But eventually an agreement was reached with the city of Delano to use the old City Hall as their home and Heritage Center.
Walter Grotz and Gene Johnson
Old Cook Stove
The Delano Franklin Township Area Historical Society was instrumental in organizing annual Heritage Festivals.

The Historical Society also organized workshops, lectures, and demonstrations, held on the first Saturday of each month. These included special recognition of Wally Grotz - Prisoner of War, The Sutton Sesquicentennial Homestead, and the 100th Anniversary of the Rieder Meat Market.

The Heritage Center became the heart of the Spirit of Community Trail, an interactive experience designed to get people to explore Delano’s historic downtown, and learn about the buildings, businesses and people who helped make Delano the community it is today.

The Society continued to be open to the public the first Saturday of each month, from 12:00-3:00. An elevator was installed in 2025, providing handicapped access to the second floor of the building, but water damage during the construction in 2024 forced the museum to close. A decision was made to renovate and restore the entire main floor during, with a targeted grand reopening in 2027. Meanwhile, the Historical Society continues to apply for and enact exhibit-related grants, accept donations, participate in community events, give presentations, and provide satellite displays at various locations in Delano.

The year 2026 was especially busy for Historical Society members as they worked with the Sesquicentennial Committee to publish a historical keepsake calendar, received a grant to print a memorial book about Delano, hosted an All-Class Reunion during the 4th of July, held monthly History Chats at the Delano Sr. Center, provided history articles for the Delano Living magazine, wrote the historical facts script for the Royal Ambassadors “Fashion Show Through the Decades” Tea Party, put together a special display for Baseball Minnesota Day, and created a slide presentation for the city’s “Happy Birthday Delano” party.

stops.title: Delano Loretto Area United Way
stops.summary: For generations, the Delano area has answered the needs of its neighbors with generosity and a strong spirit of community. What began with local business leaders and citizens joining together after World War II eventually grew into the Delano–Loretto Area United Way, part of a nationwide tradition of community-based giving. Through door-to-door campaigns, volunteer leadership, annual fundraising drives, and partnerships with local organizations, the effort has evolved along with the communities it serves. From supporting health and human-service organizations to responding to local families in need and unexpected crises, the story of the Delano–Loretto Area United Way reflects an enduring tradition: neighbors coming together to help neighbors and strengthen their community.

body.html: For generations, the Delano area has answered the needs of its neighbors with generosity and a strong spirit of community. What began with local business leaders and citizens joining together after World War II eventually grew into the Delano–Loretto Area United Way, part of a nationwide tradition of community-based giving. Through door-to-door campaigns, volunteer leadership, annual fundraising drives, and partnerships with local organizations, the effort has evolved along with the communities it serves. From supporting health and human-service organizations to responding to local families in need and unexpected crises, the story of the Delano–Loretto Area United Way reflects an enduring tradition: neighbors coming together to help neighbors and strengthen their community.

Delano giving tradition endures through time

Delano Loretto Area United Way (DLAUW) faces a world that has changed dramatically since chapter’s inception in the 1970s. A 100 years after the village of Delano was incorporated, the Delano United Way chapter was formally granted a charter by the national organization. The first United Way organization was founded in Denver in 1887. Now numbering over 1200 chapters throughout the country, United Way continues to be the largest coalition of community-based charitable fundraising in the country. Like its sister chapters across the country, the DLAUW has experienced many changes as the culture and demographics of the nation presented new challenges and new opportunities for service.

Shortly after World War II, a group of local business leaders and private citizens, who felt a sense of national pride and were inspired by new era of economic growth, founded the Delano Community Chest. A forerunner of United Way, Community Chests pooled locally-donated funds for the purpose of charitable giving. Throughout the 60s and 70s, the Community Chest grew to become Delano’s largest source of assistance for community needs as well as state and national causes. The annual campaign contributed funds to organizations such as the Lung Association, the American Cancer Society, the Sister Kenny Institute, Red Cross, the National Polio Foundation and the March of Dimes. The board of directors was comprised of representatives from clubs and organizations in the community—the churches, the American Legion and the Legion Auxiliary, chamber of commerce, school system and 4-H clubs. Board members were directly involved in fund raising. Each fall they would go door to door asking local businesses for contributions. Canisters were placed in businesses and public places for private citizens to contribute. The annual campaign was a source of community pride and was Delano’s primary philanthropic undertaking.

In the 1960s, the United Way model gained popularity across the country. Local charitable agencies could benefit from the promotional support of the national organization. In the mid-1970s, the Delano Community Chest formally became a United Way chapter. As a result of the association with the state and national organizations, Delano United Way expanded its campaign efforts to include direct marketing strategies to local citizens. In the early 2000s, the first coordinator was hired and an electronic data base and communication media were established. Because the Delano United Way serves people and agencies outside the immediate community, in the early 2000s it expanded its trade area to cover Loretto and Howard Lake to the northwest and southeast to Watertown and Mayer.

A change in giving patterns occurred in the 1990’s. There was a time when the major service organizations, such as the American Cancer Society and the March of Dimes were the primary funding requests. There occurred a proliferation of the number and variety of local charitable and service agencies. The DLAUW has responded to these requests by funding primarily local needs such as the library, senior center and city recreation programs.
   
The history of Delano is a story of people helping people, of neighbors joining together to in time of calm and crisis.  At this time of the coronavirus pandemic, the Delano Loretto Area United Way is aware is responding to this global health crisis.  DLAUW has initiated the COVID-19 Response and Recovery Fund.

stops.title: Delano Public Schools
stops.summary: The 1928 Delano School building stands as a lasting reminder of the community’s long commitment to education. Built at the corner of Elm Avenue and 2nd Street after fire damaged the earlier high school, the new building brought Delano’s grade and high school students together under one roof and was considered one of the finest and best-equipped schools in the area. Its modern gymnasium-auditorium, library, science laboratory, and industrial arts and home economics departments reflected a new era in education. As Delano grew and new schools were built, the building continued to adapt—first serving younger grades and later becoming home to Community Education and other community programs. Nearly a century after it opened, the 1928 school remains an important part of Delano’s educational and community history.

  • 1870: A two-story frame building built on corner of Bridge Avenue and 2nd Street

  • 1882: A larger school building was erected on the corner of Elm and 2nd (present site.) Destroyed by fire in 1894.

• In 1894 a new school building erected on the same site.

  • In 1903 a new high school building built directly behind the 1894 building, which then became the grade school.

• 1926: Both school buildings were damaged by a fire

  • 1927: A bond issue was passed and both the 1894 and 1903 buildings were completely taken down
Classes were held in local churches until the new building was completed.
A state-of-the-art school was built in 1928 to replace fire damaged buildings.
For the first time Delano had a regulation sized basketball court and auditorium.

• 1967: A new high school and a new grade school were built on the east campus

  • 1992: A new elementary school was built on the east campus

  • 2018: A new intermediate school was completed on the east campus

  • 2019: The 1928 building now houses the early childhood and community education program

stops.title: Funeral Services
stops.summary: Funeral customs in Delano have changed greatly since the community’s earliest days, when families prepared and cared for their loved ones at home and local carpenters often supplied the coffins. By the late 1800s and early 1900s, undertaking and embalming had become established professions, with funeral parlors gradually replacing services held in family homes. Minnesota’s first licensed woman embalmer, Mrs. Mattie Rader , was one of Delano’s early undertakers. Including Walter M. Tautges and later the Boyce Funeral Service, they provided generations of families with care during times of loss. The history of funeral services in Delano reflects not only changing customs and professions, but also the enduring role of local people and businesses in caring for their neighbors during some of life’s most difficult moments.

body.html: Funeral customs in Delano have changed greatly since the community’s earliest days, when families prepared and cared for their loved ones at home and local carpenters often supplied the coffins. By the late 1800s and early 1900s, undertaking and embalming had become established professions, with funeral parlors gradually replacing services held in family homes. Minnesota’s first licensed woman embalmer, Mrs. Mattie Rader , was one of Delano’s early undertakers. Including Walter M. Tautges and later the Boyce Funeral Service, they provided generations of families with care during times of loss. The history of funeral services in Delano reflects not only changing customs and professions, but also the enduring role of local people and businesses in caring for their neighbors during some of life’s most difficult moments.

For a long while, funeral services were held in private homes, with families caring for their dead. This began to change during the Civil War when bodies began to be embalmed.
Family funeral businesses began to spring up in communities. Many of these families were already in woodworking businesses, building furniture and coffins on request, so it was a natural transition for them to expand into full-service funeral homes. They became known as undertakers, because they “undertook” the responsibility for all the funeral arrangements. 

   In Delano, in 1881, John Coolen on River Street monopolized the furniture trade. He had been in business for five years and had always done well.  Besides furniture, he also dealt in coffins, caskets, and general undertaking.

The Delano Eagle, in 1893, promoted The Delano Furniture Co. It was composed of Messrs. N. K. Coffin and E. S. Babb, both of whom were first-class carpenters and cabinet workers.  And, “while the undertaking business is not very rushing, as the country is so healthful that there is not a great deal of illness of death except from old age, yet they are fully prepared to meet any demands for this kinds of work.”

   Newton Kimball Coffin and Elmer Sydney Babb are both enumerated in Delano on the 1895 census, occupation – furniture store. The families lived next door to each other. In 1900 they were still in Delano, occupations listed as carpenters.  N K Newton was in Delano in 1905; E. S Babb had moved to Portland, Oregon. N K moved to Washington by 1910.  Both continued as carpenters or in the building contracting business.

E. S. Redmond began a new livery stable in Delano in 1899. His ad included “Funerals Furnished Throughout”  - “I have the only Undertaking Business in Delano and have always on hand a full line of Caskets and Trimmings. A Handsome New Hearse, Mourners’ Carriages, Etc. I take full charge of Funerals and am always ready.”   He purchased the old Borsch store on the corner of River and Franklin , and moved it next to the Gilmer Hotel, with the intentions of occupying the upper rooms for a dwelling, and using the store as undertaking rooms. The Eagle reported in 1901 that E. Stacy Redmond had received word that he had passed a very satisfactory examination as an embalmer, one of only sixteen out of sixty applicants to do so.

When E. Stacy Redmond died in 1907, T. B. Rader bought his business.  T. B. Rader dealt with the undertaking goods, but his wife, Mattie Belle (nee Murphy) Rader was the embalmer.The  Delano Eagle reported in August of 1908 that “Mrs. T. B. Rader and Walter Tautges finished a course in embalming and funeral directing at the State University last week and are  now waiting for their diplomas”

Walter M. Tautges was featured in The Great Northwest Magazine , Wright County Edition, in 1909 – “The subject of this sketch, Walter M. Taugtes, established in Delano three years ago as a licensed undertaker. He has fine parlors, 2d a 5x60, the equipment of which is equal if not superior to any undertaking parlors in this section of the country – including the only hearse in the city. In this undertaking department, may be founfull line of caskets. Mr. Taugtes has devoted considerable time and attention to mastering the art of embalming and has learned a method which is pronounced by professionals as being the nearest to perfection in existence. He is kind, affectionate and full of sympathy for those in distress and ever ready to administer consolation to the afflicted. He is a good, thoughtful man in the truest sense of the word”.

Walter Tautges was born August 4, 1886, in Medina, Hennepin County. In 1905 Walter was living in Delano, working as a livery man, but by 1910 he had established his own undertaking and embalming business.  Walter married Ida .I Lohmiller Sept. 15, 1914. Walter continued as an undertaker in Delano until his death in 1925.  His widow Ida carried on the business until 1930.

Mr. and Mrs. A. J. Boyce, operators of the Boyce Funeral Service in Delano and at Waverly, succeeded the Tautges Funeral Service in 1930.  In the spring of 1941, the Peschek building was purchased by A. J. Boyce in which to house the Boyce Funeral Parlor. The Pescheck building was on River Street adjoining the Stein barber shop, and across from the current (2021) location of Delano Floral and Gifts.
They maintained a dignified funeral chapel on River Street where their display room was also located. In 1946 the Boyce Funeral Service made plans to build a Funeral Home on Third Street and Elm Avenue, where the parking problem would not be as difficult as it was in their downtown location.

The Boyce Funeral Service made plans in 1946 to build a funeral home on Third Street, where the parking problem would not be as difficult as it was in their downtown location.
James A. Iten took over the Delano funeral business in 1962, and today it is continued by his son Timothy J. Iten.

stops.title: Fire Department
stops.subtitle: Founded 1874
stops.summary: The Delano Fire Department traces its beginnings to August 1, 1876, when local residents organized the Delano Hook and Ladder Company No. 1. Over the following decades, the department grew from volunteers using hand-operated equipment into an organized community fire service with engines, hose and ladder crews, rural fire trucks, tankers, and modern equipment. Its firefighters responded to many of Delano’s most memorable disasters, including fires that destroyed schools, mills, the Delano Elevator, the Riverside Inn/American Legion Club during the 1965 flood, and the Delano Theater. The department received a new station on Second Street in 1972 and moved into another new fire station there in 2002. Today, the Firefighters Memorial outside the station, featuring Delano’s original fire bell, honors generations of firefighters whose service and dedication have protected the community for well over a century.

Early photo of the Delano Fire Department, date unknown.

The Delano Hook and Ladder Company No. 1 was the pioneer fire company in Delano. It

was organized August 1, 1876, at the home of John Steffes. The officers elected were John Steffes, William Felkner, William L. Van Eman, G. T. Mulford, E. Kurtz, John Marth, Ole O. Erwig, Daniel Fish and Valentine Eppel. A truck was made in the village at a cost of $80, and the company had its first parade on October 26.

In 1879, the Delano Hook and Ladder Company No. 1 was reorganized as the Delano Fire Company. The first officials of the new organization were John Steffes, Henry C. Parslow and Andrew Rieder.

A special election was held in February of 1880 where it was voted to lay a tax of five mills to buy a hand fire engine. When the engine arrived, however, it was not satisfactory and was not accepted.

In May of 1880 the Empire Engine and Hose Company No. 1 was organized. Officers were H. H. Blum, A. J. Willard, Swan Erickson, C.B. Moody, E. J. Swedeback and O.J. Billings.

A fire engine was purchased from the city of Mankato in 1880 for $600. The village paid the Hook and Ladder Company $200 for its truck house, ladders, truck, apparatus, and fixtures, which included all its property except the flag. The Empire Engine and Hose Company was reorganized by the village, and with the Hook and Ladder Company included in the fire department. H. Dyer was chosen chief of the fire department, and John Steffes the first assistant.

“The Village has two organized fire companies, the Delano Hook & Ladder Co., the oldest and first organized fire company in the county, and the Empire Engine & Hose Co. Both companies have each a good outfit of fire apparatus, the property of the village, and hold regular meetings for drill and business.”

(from D. R. Farnham’s History of Wright County, 1880)

In 1881, at a special election, by a vote of 25 to 6, the people voted bonds to the amount of $1,000 payable $200 annually, for the purchase of a fire engine and other apparatus.
1886 map of Downtown Delano. Fire Engine House located on the river.
Delano City Hall, built in 1888

The new city hall was built in 1888 with room for the equipment of the hook and ladder and hose and fire engine companies.

In 1896 the village council reorganized the Fire Department to have a chief, three assistants, and a fire warden. Five crews of hose men and a hook and ladder crew were begun. Each crew consisted of seven or more men. A tower was added to the city hall, and a fire bell was purchased and installed in it.
The Delano Fire Department had a treasurer’s book to keep track of expenses and payments.
Shares for outlying farms were sold in 1931, and a fire truck was purchased for the rural areas.
A new country truck was purchased in 1948, and a tanker for water was purchased for country protection.
The fire department received a new home in 1972, when a bond passed to put up a new building on Second street.
The Delano Fire Department celebrated its 100-year anniversary in 1996.
A new Delano Fire Station was built in 2002 on Second Street.
The Firefighters Memorial, in front of the current fire station, lists the names of the firemen beginning in 1896. It also features the original fire bell.

1894 – The public school house burned down.

The public school building erected in 1882 on the corner of Elm and Second burned June 1, 1894. The following article appeared in the Delano Eagle on June 7: “The old saw about “locking the stable after the horse has been stolen,” found another very apt illustration last Saturday. At the fire Friday evening the fire engine was discovered to be utterly useless through neglect and lack of usage, so on Saturday, after the damage had been all done, it was thoroughly overhauled and placed into working order. While we do not pretend to say that even under the most favorable circumstances it could have extinguished the fire in question, it is capable, with proper care and attention, of doing good work in case of an ordinary dwelling house fire, which is all that is claimed for it.”

March 15, 1900 – The A. E. Johnson & Bros. flouring mill burned down.

“At 5:30 o’clock last Friday morning the fire bell sounded the alarm. It did not take long to locate the conflagration, for the flames were pouring out at the mill. Within a few minutes the fire company was on hand and two streams were kept playing on the fire. It soon became apparent that there was nor the slightest hope of saving one of Delano’s mow important and successful business enterprises. The main building being completely enveloped in flames, the attention of the firemen was directed to the engine and boiler and their labors were not in vain for both of these expensive items, together with the boiler connections and pump, received no injury.”

January 25, 1917 – The Great Northern Hotel fire.

”One of Delano’s oldest land marks, the Great Northern Hotel, which for many years was known as Young’s Hotel, suffered damage from fire last Friday morning when the rood was discovered to be ablaze about 6:40. Those who had not already risen heard the continuous whistling of a locomotive, which after some minutes conveyed the conviction that a fire was burning and that the attention of the fire department was needed. Then, through the storm windows came the gentle tinkle of the fire bell and those in a favorable position were able to locate the conflagration. Soon great volumes of smoke curled upwards and then shot forth angry tongues of flame which leapt up many feet.” (from the Delano Eagle, February 25, 1917)

“Carpenters are making repairs to the Great Northern hotel The top story is being torn down and the building will be reduced to two stories.”
(Great Northern Hotel, Early 1900’s)
(1968 photo of building)

1921 – The Delano Milling Company burned down.

“Shortly after three o’clock last Friday morning, during the electric storm, those who were awake were startled by the fire alarm and to find the mill burning. Owing to the fact that lights and telephone were put out of commission, the alarm was not given by ‘phone and very few of the firemen were aroused. Owing to the construction of the mill and it being so dry, the fire had made considerable headway. The fire was a spectacular one and the building was totally destroyed.” (from the Delano Eagle, September 1, 1921)
(Delano Flouring Mills, Bartlett Bros.)

October 30, 1926 – the Delano 1903 High school burned.

In 1926, there was another school fire. The high school building, which had been built in 1903, was discovered to have smoke coming through the roof. The alarm was turned in, and the Delano Fire Department responded immediately, as reported in the Delano Eagle, November 4, 1926. But “right here the citizens of Delano who were under the impression that the present fire equipment was adequate were given the surprise of their life. When water was turned on it was found that the stream did not reach the roof from the ground. The ladder equipment was also found to be short. One hose furnished water, and this was carried up on adjoining buildings and due to a lack of pressure did not render the desired service. At about this time a call was put in for the Watertown fire department. In a very short time flames shot out from all portions of the roof. A strong west wind was blowing and burning shingles were carried several blocks. Bucket brigades found incipient blazes on the roofs of surrounding houses. The seriousness of the situation was greatly lessened when the high school building roof caved in. At about this time, the Watertown fire department arrived on the scene. The skeptics were still skeptical until the pumper commenced to operate. The pumper shot a heavy stream of water which demonstrated clearly that had we a like apparatus the fire would have been put out with but little damage to the roof. The Delano fire department fought valiantly but were severely handicapped. When it was discovered that they could do nothing with the high school fire they contented themselves by saving the adjoining grade building dragging the only line of hose in service on top of the building and confining the loss to a partially burned roof in the northeast corner.

February 1, 1932 – Keplinger’s Red & White Store Damaged by Fire

The Delano Eagle reported “A fire which completely baffled the Delano Fire department broke out in the Red & White store, owned by Mrs. A. M. Keplinger, Monday night at about eleven o’clock. It was one of the most stubborn fires which has confronted the local fire department in years. There was no blaze to be found, but huge billows of smoke poured out of the front and back doors and through portions of the roof. The smoke was so thick that no one could enter, and the department had to be content to fight the fire from the front and rear parts of the building. Three streams of water were poured into the building from the time the fire was discovered until near daybreak. “
March 28, 1962 – Fire destroyed the Delano Elevator Company elevator and grinding mill. It was the biggest fire in Delano since the flour mill burned in the 1921.

April, 1965 – The Riverside Inn/ American Legion Club building burned during the flood.

“An ironic occurrence during the flood was the complete destruction of the Legion Club on Highway 12 by fire. Because of the flood waters, which completely surrounded the building, the fire department was unable to reach the scene.”
April 27, 1971 – The Delano Theater burned down. It was a four-alarm fire, and the building was a total loss.

1992 – The grandstand at the ballpark was burned down to make room for a new one.

An end of an era was reached Wednesday evening, September 23, when the Delano Fire Department burned down the Delano grandstand that had been a fixture in Delano since 1935. The council ordered the grandstand demolished because it was a safety hazard.
2006 – Stein’s barber shop of River Street was burned down in a controlled burn.

stops.title: Leiter’s Livery and Auto
stops.address: SE corner of Bridge Ave. and 2nd St.
stops.summary: The corner of Bridge and Second streets tells a remarkable story of Delano’s changing transportation, business, and community life. From schoolhouse and livery barn to automobile garage, factory, civic center, and commercial corner, this site reflects more than a century of change in the heart of Delano.

body.html: The corner of Bridge and Second streets tells a remarkable story of Delano’s changing transportation, business, and community life. From schoolhouse and livery barn to automobile garage, factory, civic center, and commercial corner, this site reflects more than a century of change in the heart of Delano.
The building in the background is the old two-story frame school which was moved to the corner of Bridge and Second streets. The Swedish Mission church can be seen in the far background.
This photos shows both the livery barn in the background, and the new brick building for Leiter’s Auto business.

In 1910, Frank Leiter’s occupation was listed as the proprietor of a livery. The 1915 History of Wright County, Vol II, lists Frank Leiter as having a livery service, with Frank Leiter and Milo J Hall proprietors of an automobile garage.

In 1870 a two-story frame school building was erected at the corner of Elm and Second streets. That building was moved to the corner of Second and Bridge streets when a new brick school building was erected in 1882.
The frame building was bought by F. A. Flood, who dealt in general farm machinery. A pen sketch drawn in 1898 of the Delano businesses shows a cigar factory in the building.

But in May of 1908, Leiter and Walker announced that they were ”now occupying our new home opposite the city hall and have added new rigs and horses to our equipment and are ready to accommodate the public with first-class, up-to-date turnouts. When in need of livery give us a trial. Will do our best to please you and treat you right.”
Home Motors and Case dealer, on the corner of Bridge and Second streets.
From the “Mainstreet’ special edition, 1946

Takor Inc. purchased the Leiter Garage building in September of 1959. They did an extensive remodeling of the existing building and the construction of a new adjoining building in 1962.  The company manufactured photo developing tanks and other items out of plastic.
The building was again remodeled, and became the city offices, senior center, and off and on sale municipal liquor store from 1983 - 2003.
It was torn down in 2003, and a new commercial building erected by the city. The corner currently houses Brickside Grill and Tap, American Farm Insurance, and Fran Stein’s barbershop.
American Farm Insurance, Stein’s Barber Shop, Brickside Grill and Tap- 2021
Ironically, the current City Hall  and Senior Center now stand where Leiter’s livery barn once stood, on the northeast corner of Second and Bridge.

stops.title: Sesquicentennial
stops.subtitle: Delano 150th · 1876-2026
stops.summary: Delano was founded in 1876 along the banks of the Crow River. What started as a small river town has grown into the community you're standing in today, built by generations who showed up for each other. In 2026, Delano celebrated 150 years the way this town does everything: together. The celebration kicked off with a "150 Ways to Celebrate" campaign, giving the town 150 reasons to get involved throughout the year.

body.html:
Delano was founded in 1876 along the banks of the Crow River. What started as a small river town has grown into the community you're standing in today, built by generations who showed up for each other.

In 2026, Delano celebrated 150 years the way this town does everything: together. The celebration kicked off with a "150 Ways to Celebrate" campaign, giving the town 150 reasons to get involved throughout the year.
A few of the 150 Ways to Celebrate…
Delano's Sesquicentennial: Delano Turns 150
A historic 2026 calendar, filled with old photos and milestone dates from Delano's past, was given out free to the community thanks to local sponsors.
On February 11th, Delano's actual birthday, signs along Highway 12 were changed for the day to read "Happy Birthday, Delano," and the community gathered at City Hall to celebrate.
At the Chamber of Commerce "I Love Delano Dinner," city council members reenacted the original signing of the Delano Corporation, bringing the town's founding moment back to life.

On June 13, the Delano Area Council for Arts and Culture’s Sculpture and Blues Fest gave Delano something permanent. A new sculpture, created by James and Ryan Pedersen, stands as the centerpiece: four pillars representing the Crow River, agriculture, industry, and the railroad, with the number 150 formed in the space between them. A mural by Leanna Wurzer weaves in photos of over 2,000 tiles decorated by the community, and a path of Heritage Bricks are dedicated with personal messages to families, businesses, and organizations that make up Delano.
Local author Marcia Brakke published Delano on the Crow: 150 Years of Unrivaled Spirit, launched at the book at an elegant evening at the Jerome in June.

As home of the largest Fourth of July celebration in Minnesota, our celebration was one to remember marking both the nation's 250th birthday and the Delano's 150th in the same year, complete with a Delano 150 float in the parade!
It all came together on October 3rd at the Delano 150 Years Jamboree, a full day of music, food, and celebration that closed with the whole town singing "Happy Birthday" together.
Here's to the next 150 years, Delano!
The content of this page is brought to you by the Delano Spirit of Community Trail Committee in honor of Delano's 150th Anniversary.

stops.title: Delano Village Hall
stops.subtitle: Built in 1988
stops.summary: Built in 1888, Delano’s Village Hall quickly became much more than the place where local government conducted its business—it became the heart of community life. The building housed village offices, the fire department, and even a jail, while its upstairs hall welcomed dances, school graduations, basketball games, church dinners, weddings, funerals, and theatrical performances. A stage and dressing rooms were added as entertainment flourished, followed by the familiar tower and fire bell in 1896 and jail cells in 1905. Over the years, the building also provided space for the public library and local elections. Through generations of meetings, celebrations, public service, and everyday gatherings, Delano’s historic City Hall has played a central role in the civic and social life of the community.

The building housed village offices, the fire department, and even a jail, while its upstairs hall welcomed dances, school graduations, basketball games, church dinners, weddings, funerals, and theatrical performances. A stage and dressing rooms were added as entertainment flourished, followed by the familiar tower and fire bell in 1896 and jail cells in 1905. Over the years, the building also provided space for the public library and local elections. Through generations of meetings, celebrations, public service, and everyday gatherings, Delano’s historic City Hall has played a central role in the civic and social life of the community.
Since 1888 the Village Hall has served as the Delano City Government building, Fire Station, Police Station with a jail, plus Theater, Events Hall and the Public Library.
Every event we host is designed with intention, from the atmosphere we create to the way each session flows.
A two story out-house was attached to the back of Village Hall, women above and men below.
Two Story Outhouse in the background of this photo

• 1887: The idea of building a Village Hall in Delano began to grow in the minds of the Village Council and the citizens of the town. Mr. Breed donated two lots for the site. A special election decides to spend $3,000 for a Village Hall. Brick for the building was purchased from Ziebarth's brick factory located along the Crow River in Franklin Township.

  • 1888: The 4th of July celebration that year was said to have been the most successful ever undertaken. "The large upstairs hall was comfortably filled with 200 couples. The beautiful maple floor was spacious and accommodating." On September 19th the celebration of the completion of Village Hall included a grand parade, dance and supper under the auspices of the Delano Fire Department.

  • 1890: A stage with dressing rooms on each side was built for the Delano Dramatic Company and other traveling theatrical performances.

  • 1896: A tower was built for the fire bell. This fire bell is now displayed in front of the present fire hall.

• 1977: The Fire Department moved to a new building. The Delano Public Library now shared Village Hall with City Offices.

  • 1983: City Offices moved out of Village Hall to their own building.

  • 2004: Village Hall is now used for the Delano Franklin Township Area Heritage Center
Village Hall is the Delano Franklin Township Heritage Center Today

stops.title: Barbers
stops.summary: Barber shops have been a familiar part of Delano’s business community since the town’s earliest years. By 1881, Reynold M. Bohn was serving local customers, and over the decades barbers including Charles Parnell, Beverly C. Yancey, the Bock brothers, Leslie Krumm, and others operated shops along River Street, Franklin Avenue, and Bridge Avenue. Among the longest-lasting traditions was the Stein family’s barbering business: Armand Stein began working in a barber shop as a boy in 1912, eventually opening his own shop, and his son Fran joined the profession in 1967. When Stein’s Barber Shop moved to Bridge Avenue in 2006, historic fixtures—including an 1800s backbar, 1917 barber chairs, and a hand-cranked barber pole—went with it, preserving a tangible connection to more than a century of Delano barbering history.

body.html: Barber shops have been a familiar part of Delano’s business community since the town’s earliest years. By 1881, Reynold M. Bohn was serving local customers, and over the decades barbers including Charles Parnell, Beverly C. Yancey, the Bock brothers, Leslie Krumm, and others operated shops along River Street, Franklin Avenue, and Bridge Avenue. Among the longest-lasting traditions was the Stein family’s barbering business: Armand Stein began working in a barber shop as a boy in 1912, eventually opening his own shop, and his son Fran joined the profession in 1967. When Stein’s Barber Shop moved to Bridge Avenue in 2006, historic fixtures—including an 1800s backbar, 1917 barber chairs, and a hand-cranked barber pole—went with it, preserving a tangible connection to more than a century of Delano barbering history.

1881 – September 15, The Delano Eagle

BARBER – “R. Bohn fills the tonsorial bill for Delano, and his patrons all claim that his work is exceeding good. He has been in Delano since 1879, and came here from Sweden. Delano is well able to support a barber, and Mr. Bohn is never short of custom.”

1885 – January 1, The Delano Eagle

BARBER SHOPS – “Mr. R. Bohn and Mr. Chas. Parnell attend to the tonsorial wants of our citizens; the former’s place of business being on River Street, the latter’s on Franklin Avenue.”

(from the Delano Eagle, August 28, 1890)

“Mr. R. M. Bohn is negotiating for the purchase of I. H. Grafft’s store building on River Street. He intends to use the from room on the lower floor for a hair-dressing room, and the back part of the same story for bath rooms. The upstairs will be remodeled and converted into a photograph gallery by using the glass roof now on the present photograph gallery building which Mr. Bohn intends to convert into a residence. Mr. Bohn made an offer for the building some time ago, but it was not accepted until last week.”

Reynold M. Bohn was born March 4, 1850 in Norway, and immigrated to America in 1879. According to the 1880 census, he was boarding with the Nicholas Begon family on Railroad Avenue in Delano; he was 30 years old, single, and a barber. He married, but his wife committed suicide in 1883. R.M. married Frances A Cebulla on Aug. 23, 1888 in St. Paul. The 1895 census for Delano lists him as a barber and music teacher. In 1900, R.M., his wife Frances, and their four children, Frances Angela, Oscar F., Grover C. L, and Henrietta, were living in Delano; his occupation was listed as barber. R. M. died October 7, 1904, and is buried in the Delano Cemetery. His tombstone is engraved with a musical lyre.

Grover Bohn followed in his father’s footsteps. He began his lifetime career in high school of both barbering and the musical profession, which he followed until his retirement in 1958 after barbering for 49 years. Grover moved to Colorado in 1920, as a veteran to WWI, where he was the assistant band leader of the 358th Infantry Band of the 90th Division.
(Frances A. Bohn married Henry Stein, the brother of Armand Stein, -see below)
(Ads from the Delano Eagle, 1891
Charles Parnell is enumerated on the 1885 Minnesota State Census as living in Delano, with his wife Alice, and their children Laura, Mollie, and Chas.
“The barbers of Delano are Wm. Cowl, Wm. Seippel, Wm. Cuttler, and Wm. Banteon. Now ‘Will” you get shaved.” (from the Delano Eagle, April 5, 1906)

Beverly C. Yancey was a barber in Delano from at least 1895 through 1920. His shop was located on River Street, approximately in the location of the current vacant lot next to Rieder’s Meat Market. B.C. was enumerated either as a black or a mulatto on the census records. In 1895 and 1900 his nephew, Edward Brown was living with him and in 1900 Edward ‘s occupation also was listed as barber.
B.C. Yancy in his shop.

from The Great Northwest Magazine, December 1909:

“If there is any time more than another when a man feels that life is a dream of bliss, it is when he undergoes the soothing manipulation of a first class barber such as Mr. B. C. Yancey, the popular barber, has proven himself to be. Mr. Yancey, though a resident of Delano for more than seventeen years, did not, until last fall, actively unite himself with the business men of Delano. He is established in an up-to-date shop, in size 16x24. Diligent attention and earnest endeavor to steadily grow in his profession has placed him in the lie with many tonsorial artists of a life-long experience. One always finds him in good spirits, happy and jolly. He has become a favorite, as shown by the very large trade he has worked up in so short a period of time. It truly speaks well for the man and his skill in the manipulation of the razor.”

Bock Brothers

Three brothers, Charlie, Emil, and August Bock owned a barber shop together in Delano.

“We have moved from the old barber shop stand into C. M. Conzet’s building where the light will be sufficient to enable us to do first-class work, and we have our shop in first-class shape and ready for business. We have added a bath room to our shop and are ready to serve both ladies and gentlemen with baths. Call and see us in our new quarters. BOCK BROS. (from The Delano Eagle, October 10, 1907)
August Bock, Hamilton in chair; Charlie Bock, Fred Bock in chair; Armand Stein in chair, Carl “Rooster Eckman”, and Eddie Bock.

From the Delano Eagle, 1955:

Charley Bock Has Been Barber for 50 Years

Charley Bock started his barbering with Bev Yancy in June 1905. He had never gone to barber school or served an apprenticeship. His first day in Yancey’s shop he started out by giving shaves and haircuts. “I did a lot of that kind of work for my friends and relatives before I went to work in the shop and I guess Bev thought that was apprenticeship enough”, Charley said.

Charley worked for Yancy for 10 months and then took a job with Billy Cowles for six months. He worked in St. Paul and Billings, Montana before coming back to Delano and buying out the Cowles shop and going into business for himself.

During the time he was barbering in Delano, Charley taught the trade to six barbers: Carl Eckman; Armand Stein; Edward DeNoon; E. H. Bock, a nephew; Milo Bock, his son; and Carl Weldele.
Charley Bock, cutting the hair of Frank Kaeppe. Frank was one of Charley’s first customers when he started barbering in Delano in 1905.

Carl Eckman

The Delano Eagle reported in November of 1909 that Carl Eckman, who had been working in Washington for a few months, would be arriving back in Delano and soon be barbering in W. B. Seippel’s shop. Several years later, in 1925, the Eagle noted that he had moved his shop into the building recently vacated by Lembke’s Economy store on Bridge Street, and that “it was a great improvement over the old one.” (That building is currently the Book Nook.) Carl “Rooster” Eckman worked with Armand Stein for many years.

Armand Stein

Armand was the youngest son of John Louis Stein, an early saloonist in Delano and one of the builders of the brick block building on Bridge Street. “Armand started working in the barber shop in 1912. He was eight years old, and started off by shining shoes and lathering faces for shaves. During World War I, there was a shortage of barbers in Delano, because the majority of the barbers went to work in defense plants for the war effort. Armand’s brother-in-law, Charlie Bock, took him to the governor, and the governor granted the 15-year-old his license.” (from the Delano Eagle, September 11, 2006)

Armand moved out to the west coast in in 1922. After a few years of barbering in California, in San Francisco and Hollywood, Armand returned to Minnesota and opened his shop in Delano.
Armand married Adeline Horsch; their son Francis continued in his father’s business in the same location on River Street.
Fran Stein started barbering with his father Armand in 1967. He went on to barber full-time for fifty-eight years. In 2006 Fran moved his shop to a new location across from the Delano City Hall.

The history of Stein’s Barber Shop did not end when it moved. The backbar, from the 1800s; chairs, bought new in 1917; and the hand-cranked barber pole, only one or two of those types of barber poles left in the country, accompanied Fran on the move.

“Krumm’s Barber and Beauty Shop, located on the corner of Bridge and River Street, Delano, was owned and operated by Mr. and Mrs. Leslie Krumm, who took over the business from Mr. and Mrs. Ed Bock in 1941. For nine years, before coming to Delano, Mr. and Mrs. Krumm operated a barber and shop at 5460 Nicollet Ave., Minneapolis.” (from the 1946 The Eagle presents Delano, Minnesota)

The shop was in the same building where the Bock Brother barbered in 1907.
Mr. Leslie Krumm daughter Ihla Rae; Mrs. Krumm with customer, 1946

Dennis Kettenacker opened a barber shop in that same building in 1961. He was killed in a car-train crash in 1966, and Lowell McKinley bought the shop in 1967. He eventually sold it and went on to work in Excelsior, Maple Plain, and Victoria, before coming back to Delano. In 2022 Lowell McKinley joined Fran working out of Stein’s Barber Shop on Bridge Avenue. Lowell and Fran had known each other since 1966, but this was the first time they worked together. Fran sold his shop in 2025, and it the new owners opened Wright Cuts.

stops.title: Bakeries
stops.summary: Bakeries have been a familiar part of Delano’s business community for well over a century. One of the earliest was operated by Napoleon Hamel , who moved to Delano in 1902 and became known for a modern, well-equipped bakery offering breads, cakes, pies, pastries, and other baked goods, some of which were shipped to neighboring communities. He continued in the bakery business until his death in 1927. Other bakeries followed, including the Delano Home Town Bakery, Palm’s Bakery, and Roy and Mrs. Hanson’s bakery, which by 1946 was Delano’s only retail bakery. Perhaps the best remembered was the Delano Bakery , opened by Kerney and Genevieve Jacobson in 1948. For nearly 40 years, the couple produced countless loaves of bread, hundreds of thousands of doughnuts, and thousands of decorated cakes, building a loyal following that extended well beyond Delano. The original bakery closed in 1988, but the Delano Bakery name continued in a new location—almost on the same site where Napoleon Hamel had operated his bakery generations earlier.

(from The Great Northwestern Magazine, December 1909)

Napoleon Hamel “We believe that no town of the size of Delano can boast of a cleaner, more attractive and more modern bakery than you have right here. People who are acquainted with Napoleon Hamel and who have occasion to patronize him always remark that his place is one of the cleanest, most inviting and up to date that they have seen. Besides this the store and shop are large and finely equipped and only the best of goods are handled. Mr. Hamel has been established here for the past seven years, although he has had much more experience in this line, and during that time he has always met the demands of the public in the most satisfactory manner. He carries an excellent stock of the choicest cakes, pies, pastries, rolls and baker’s goods of every variety. He ships goods of this nature to Watertown, Waverly and Montrose. He is prompt and courteous in attending to his patrons, and employs only the most competent and obliging help. He is a man of honest convictions, more than ordinary discernment and business enterprise and sagacity.”

(from the History of Wright County Minnesota Volume II 1915)

The brief business directory lists Napoleon Hamel, baker.

Napoleon Hamel was born in Quebec, Canada in 1872; he immigrated to the United States and Minnesota in 1886. The Minneapolis City Directories for 1890 and 1891 list Napoleon as a cook in the French Hotel. Napoleon was working as a cook in Minneapolis in the 1895 census. The Minneapolis Directories for 1899 and 1900 show that he was in the restaurant business at 1009 Washington Avenue N. Napoleon married Virginia Scott on August 23, 1897, in Hennepin County. The couple moved to Delano in 1902, and the 1905 census lists Napoleon as a baker. He continued to have a bakery in Delano until he passed away September 23, 1927. Napoleon and Virginia had four children: Bernadette Angela, Pearl Alice, Marie Eugenie, and Joseph Napoleon. Bernadette married Edward Henry Dunn; their daughter Virginia married Clarence “Buzz” Matter. Pearl married Alvin C Weihe in 1936. Marie married Francis Harney, and Joseph married Mary T. Kelly. Napoleon’s wife Virginia passed away in 1925; she and Napoleon are buried in Calvary Cemetery in Delano.
Ad from the Delano Eagle, Sept. 26, 1926
The Delano Home Town Bakery opened in September 1930, next to the (old) City Hall. Swanberg and Cox, proprietors.
This ad appeared in the Delano Eagle in April 1933.
(Ads from the Delano Eagle, March, 1933)

(from the Special Edition - The Eagle, 1946)

“Mr. and Mrs. Roy Hanson have operated for the past 15 years. Starting on Third Street in 1933, after a few months they moved downtown where they have since been located. Presently the bakery is situated next door to Marshall-wells store. It is currently the only retail bakery in Delano.”
Hanson’s Bakery, 1946
This building is the Ziebarth/Lebovsky Block. It currently houses, in 2026, DownTown Social. Hanson’s Bakery was in the south half of the building.
New Delano Bakery Will Be Ready for Business Saturday

“The new Delano bakery next to the city hall will open for business on Saturday, May 8, according to the owner, Mr. Hilmer Hansen. Mr. Hansen, who came here from Hutchinson where he had been operating a bakery for his father, has had many years’ experience in the bakery business. Something a little different in the line of bakery goods will be offered in the Danish Kringle. This according to Mr. Hansen, looks like a giant pretzel but is a form of coffee cake.”
The building next to city hall was a bakery for several years, with several different proprietors, but became a Red Owl store in 1940.
Kerney and Genevieve Jacobson opened the Delano Bakery in 1948.
The Delano Bakery

Cornelius ("Kerney") and Genevieve Jacobson first opened the original Delano Bakery in 1948.  Kerney was a cook in the army during World War II, and upon returning from the war, he and his wife, Gen, along with their 4-year-old son, Dale, opened the famous “Delano Bakery” in Delano, Minnesota.  

The bakery quickly became very successful, and for the next 40 years, Kerney and Gen made countless loaves of bread for all the schools in the area, hundreds of thousands of doughnuts for all their regular customers from locals to non-locals, and thousands of beautifully decorated cakes for graduations, birthdays, and especially weddings.   Kerney would do all the baking and Genevieve would decorate as many as 15+ wedding cakes in a single weekend.  In over 40 years, neither of them missed a single day of work.   They stayed very busy and the bakery only continued to become more well known and well-respected.  Genevieve remembers the day she realized they had baked over one million loaves of bread.

The original Delano Bakery remained open for almost 40 years before finally closing its doors in 1988, when Dale and his family moved from Delano to Forest Lake, Minnesota. (historical information from www.thedelanobakery.com)

The Delano Bakery was located on the corner of Bridge Avenue and Second Street. The small pocket park, next to Joe McDonald’s Photography Studio. (The Delano Bakery is the two-story building with the outside staircase in the left of this 1963 photo.)

When the Delano Bakery closed on the corner of Bridge and Second, it opened in a new building around the corner, between Bridge and Railroad avenues. Interestingly, that was almost in the same location where Napoleon Hamel had his bakery.

stops.title: Beck Building
stops.subtitle: Built 1912
stops.summary: The Beck Building at 136 Bridge Avenue E. , built by John M. Beck in 1912 next to Delano’s original City Hall, has housed an unusually diverse collection of businesses during its more than century-long history. Beck, a music teacher and director of the Delano Band, originally used the building for his music and stationery business, while his daughter Clotildis “Claudia” Beck operated a photography studio there and created an important visual record of early Delano. Later occupants included the Delano Granite and Marble Works, several bakeries, the Red Owl grocery store, Ditty Plumbing and Heating, and the Delano Family Dental Clinic. Cutting Edge Construction moved into the historic building in 2005, and portions of the early construction added by monument maker Bert Gilmer can still be seen at the rear. In 2026, the storefront was occupied by Western Creations , continuing the Beck Building’s long tradition of adapting to the changing businesses of downtown Delano.

John M. Beck built the building next to the original city hall in 1912.  Over the years it has held many businesses.

J. M. Beck was a music teacher, and served as the director of the Delano Band, as well as directing the choir of St, Peter’s church during the years the family lived in Delano. He built the store for his music and stationary business.
John M Beck, was the director of the Military Band, is in the center of the front row.
His daughter, Clotildis (Claudia) Beck, also had a photography studio in the building.​

body.html: 1919 - The building is now housing the Delano Granite and Marble Works.​

Bert Gilmer opened a monument shop in Delano in 1917, and bought the building in 1919. He added a tower to the back of the building to handle the pieces of granite. When Clarence Dunn joined the firm in 1925, the Delano Granite offices were still in the building next to the city hall on Bridge Avenue.  He reminisced about looking out the only window in the place - right into the jail next door.

In September of 1930, Mr. H. Swanberg of Chicago and Mr. Cox rented the Bert Gilmer building next to city hall and re-arranged the interior for the manufacture and sale of bakery products. It was promoted as a new business industry for Delano.
The building continued to be a bakery:
The Red Owl Agency was in the building next to the City Hall in 1940, operated by William Kirsch. When he died in April of that year, his wife, Ella, sold the business to Lawrence and Alice Karl.
Mr. and Mrs. Karl operated the Red Owl store for six years, and then sold it to Raymond C. Trueman.  Mr.Trueman died in 1952.
Ditty Plumbing and Heating was located in the building the 60’s.
Ditty Plumbing and Heating was located in the building the 60’s.

Beginning in 1987, Tom Madden, opened his dentistry office in this building.  In 1988 his brother Mark joined him.  They remained at this address until 2004, when they built a new office on Elm Avenue by Delano Public Schools.

In 2005 Cutting Edge Construction, moved to Delano and into the Beck building. Michael Anastasia, who was joined in 1991 by his brother Pete, started the company in 1985 in Long Lake. The business has completed hundreds of commercial restaurant and bar projects and a variety of projects for retailers, service firms, and non-profit organizations, including a number of projects involving historical building and renovation in historical districts in the Minnesota area. Pete Anastasia is the current president of the company and owner of this historical building in Delano, where it is still possible to see some of the original construction added by Bert Gilmer in the back of the building.
Western Creations was in the building in March of 2026, and in September of the same year it transitioned to …….

stops.title: Brick Block on Bridge
stops.summary: Built in 1905 on Bridge Avenue , Delano’s Brick Block Building was an ambitious two-story brick commercial building created by Olof Peterson, Louis and Henry Bock, and John L. Stein. Its 100-foot frontage was divided among Peterson’s shoe store, Stein’s business, and a large center section intended for a department store. Before construction was even complete, the center became a gathering place for plays, dances, and community events and later housed businesses and institutions ranging from Kelly & Murray’s department store and the Delano Café to the post office, Picus clothing store, and Rainbow Inn. Over the decades, other portions of the block were home to Heinen Hardware, the Comet Theater, Boyce Funeral Home, Jack’s Food Guild, and the Coast-to-Coast Store, illustrating the building’s central role in generations of Delano commerce and community life. By 2019, the historic building had entered another chapter with The Refoundry and the newly remodeled Jerome Event Center , continuing the Brick Block’s more than century-long presence in downtown Delano.

Its 100-foot frontage was divided among Peterson’s shoe store, Stein’s business, and a large center section intended for a department store. Before construction was even complete, the center became a gathering place for plays, dances, and community events and later housed businesses and institutions ranging from Kelly & Murray’s department store and the Delano Café to the post office, Picus clothing store, and Rainbow Inn. Over the decades, other portions of the block were home to Heinen Hardware, the Comet Theater, Boyce Funeral Home, Jack’s Food Guild, and the Coast-to-Coast Store, illustrating the building’s central role in generations of Delano commerce and community life. By 2019, the historic building had entered another chapter with The Refoundry and the newly remodeled Jerome Event Center, continuing the Brick Block’s more than century-long presence in downtown Delano.

A handsome business building was erected on Bridge avenue in 1905 by Olaf Peterson, Louis and Henry Bock, and John L. Stein. The plans were drafted by Swan Erickson and called for a solid brick structure with a 100-foot front, 90 feet deep, full basement, plate front, two stories above ground, heating plant for the entire building and all modern conveniences. Mr. Peterson’s shoe store would occupy the east 25x90 end, John Stein’s business the west 25x90 end, and the center room, 50x90, would be rented for a department store.

Five brick masons and five tenders began laying the brick in June of 1905; the work went fast, finishing in eight months!

Ole Peterson occupied his section (the east end) of the new building beginning in September 1905. Mr. Peterson was a shoemaker. He was born in Sweden, where he learned his trade until 25 years of age. He emigrated to the United States and moved to Delano in December of 1869. Mr. Peterson was still listed as the owner of a retail shoe store in Delano on the 1910 census. It was said he carried one of the most extensive lines of boots and shoes found outside of the larger cities.

Peterson’s remaining stock was sold out in 1913; He died January 17, 1914. Berner Blomquist moved his furniture store into Ole’s Bockman’s building, which was Ole Peterson’s building after adding a balcony to accommodate part of his stock. (Ole Bockman was Ole Peterson’s son-in-law)

Heinen Hardware moved into this location in 1933 and remained there until it closed in 1991.

Kevin Lindquist then bought the building and opened a custom framing store. The building later was the home of Delano Floral and Gifts, followed by a school spirit wear business for Delano and surrounding districts. The Refoundry opened in the building in 2019.The building was sold in 2025, and currently is the home of The Vintage Storyteller.

The center section of the brick block belonged to the Bocks. Although the entire building was not completed, it was secured by the Dramatic Club for its grand production of “The Deserter” for the Fourth of July of 1905. A large stage was erected, and the site was wired for electric lights.

The space seems to have been used as an center for about the first year and a half. A grand ball was held in October of 1905, with the crowd enjoying the hard maple floor, large room and first-class accommodations.

A masquerade ball in Bock’s building on February 21, 1906, was described as one of the best Delano had ever seen… “the magnificent hall was brilliantly lighted and beautifully decorated, with gaily dressed masqueraders winding in and out through the giddy maze.”

Finally, Kelly & Murray, of Waverly, rented Bock’s store building in January of 1907. They opened their large general merchandise store in March. L.R. Kelly bought out Kelly & Murray in 1910, and then in 1913 closed the store and sold out all the remaining merchandise.
The Kelly & Murray Store, 1909
The second-floor space was used for offices and living quarters.
In 1917 the center of the brick block building housed the post office, with Henry J. Bock as the postmaster, and a restaurant, the Delano Café.

Wm. Picus bought the Bock building in 1921 in the section that had been the Delano Café and opened a department store. The American Legion located their club rooms above Picus’ store in 1928. Vennett Beauty Shop was located over the Picus store when the American Legion moved. Angie’s Beauty Shop was located on the street level from 1937-1943, succeeded by Mella-Dor Beauty Box., and Then Kitty’s Beauty Shop until 1948.

In 1957 Ed and Marge Andres and their children moved to Delano, and opened a Coast-to-Coast.

Store . Son Jerome, having completed four years in the U. S. Navy, entered the business with his parents in 1971. Jerome owned and expanded the store until 2005, when it was bought by Chris Johnson who moved the business out to Highway 12.

The Rainbow Inn was in the center of the brick block in 1946, next to Heinen Hardware. It was owned and operated by Robert Nicolai and Mr. and Mrs. Everett Zabel. Serving beer, soft drinks and refreshments, it was a popular spot for light lunches. The Rainbow was later operated by Bud and Colleen DeMaris. The Rainbow Inn section of the Brick Block was later part of the Coast to Coast store.

The fourth section (the west end) of the brick block was built by John L. Stein, who died in October of 1906, soon after the building was completed. His wife Josephine inherited the building, and the contents of a saloon. The Comet Theater, run by his son-in-law Ed Probst, was in that location for several years. The Boyce Funeral Home occupied the site just before Jack Schumacher bought the building from the Stein estate in 1941, remodeled the front and moved his Jack Sprat store there.
The Brick Block building 2019

stops.title: East Brick Block on Bridge
stops.subtitle: Built 1905
stops.summary: The east end of Delano’s Brick Block at 137 Bridge Avenue E. has served the community through more than a century of changing businesses. Built in 1905 by Olof Peterson in partnership with Henry and Louis Bock and John L. Stein, the property’s early history was connected to Peterson’s shoe store and later to several furniture businesses. In 1933, William Heinen moved his hardware store into the building, where Heinen Hardware remained for 58 years , until 1991. The building later housed Kevin Linquist’s custom framing shop, and its upstairs apartment even appeared as a filming location in the 1998 movie A Simple Plan . More recent occupants have included Delano Floral and Gifts and The Refoundry. After another sale and the naming of the building as the Delano Brick Block , The Vintage Storyteller opened there in May 2026 , continuing the building’s long tradition as a downtown Delano business location.

The Brick Block building on Bridge Avenue was built in 1905 by Olof Peterson in conjunction with Henry and Louis Bock and John L. Stein. Olof Peterson had come to Crow River (Delano) in 1869 and opened a shoe store. His business, from at least 1894, was just to the east of the brick block. Olof retired in 1913 and died in 1914; his building went to his son-in-law, Ole Backman.
Berner Bloomquist moved his furniture business into that space in March 1917, adding additional space by erecting a balcony.

In 1919 John Berlin tore out the west wall of the old shoe store stand and connected it to his present store in the brick block.

John Lohmiller had a furniture store in the building until September 1933, when the building was sold.

In 1933 William Heinen moved his hardware store from River Street to the east end of the brick block building. Heinen Hardware remained there for 58 years, until 1991.

Kevin Linquist bought the building and opened a custom framing shop.

The apartment upstairs was used for Bill Bob Thornton’s character’s apartment in the 1998 movie “A Simple Plan.”

Delano Floral and Gifts was in the building from 2000-2015

From 2019 to 2025, The Refoundry, a store specializing in repurposed furniture and home accessories, occupied the building. The building was again sold and was named the Delano Brick Block. In May 2026 the Vintage Storyteller opened in that location.

stops.title: Eppel Building
stops.subtitle: Moved to current location in 1871
stops.summary: The Eppel Building at 100 Bridge Avenue E. , at the corner of Bridge Avenue and River Street, is one of Delano’s oldest surviving commercial landmarks. Its history reaches back to 1871 , when Charles Eppel moved the building from south of the railroad tracks to its present location and opened a mercantile store selling dry goods and groceries along with a saloon. The building had also been the Eppel family home, where the first Catholic Mass in the community was celebrated by a missionary priest. Over the years, additions were made and the property housed a harness shop and an early restaurant operated by Charles’s son Leo. During much of the 20th century, the building became closely associated with Curley’s Men’s Clothing Store , later operated by Marshall Dainsberg and then Carroll Lundeen. Since the clothing store closed, numerous businesses have occupied the building, including Linnea’s Ice Cream Parlor, Curves for Women, Cyber Geeks, Bridge House Coffee & Café and Nature Nook Cafe and Wine Bar. Although its exterior has been extensively remodeled, the building retains its original form and remains recognizable as the structure Charles Eppel moved to this prominent downtown corner more than 150 years ago.

• This building at 100 Bridge Ave. E. was originally located near the present site of St. Peter's church. It was the home of Charles Eppel and his family.

  • The first mass in the town was read by a missionary priest in this house.

  • In 1871, Charles moved his building to its present location and opened a mercantile store and saloon. Additions were made to accommodate a harness shop.

• Charles' son, Leo opened his first restaurant in the back room of the saloon.

  • In the early 20th century the Eppel building became Curley's Clothing Store. It was sold to Carroll Lundeen and became Lundeen's.
In 1998 the building was used during the filming of “A Simple Plan” staring Bill Paxton, Billy Bob Thornton and Bridget Fonda.

Several businesses have occupied the building, including a China and Crystal business, Linnea's Ice Cream Parlor, Curves for Women, Cyber Geeks, Wilbur’s Coffee and currently Nature Nook Cafe and Wine Bar.
